findings.reason: §3 is the document's normative core; it must add the `gates` row and a §4 template or it teaches an incomplete contract that the write guard (`_SECTION_RECOGNISED_SPELLING`, `reckon/_plan_html.py:1270`) and read warning will later refuse, which is the misparse class this plan exists to prevent.
findings.text: §3 claims to enumerate "every tag, and WHY" for the machine-readable contract but lists five body sections; `reckon/_plan_html.py:190` defines six (`SECTION_IDS = ("gates", "decisions", "followups", "questions", "research", "comments")`) and `reckon/_plan_html.py:1271` gives `gates` its canonical spelling `<div class="r-gate" data-id="...">`; §4 supplies a copy-paste template for every section except `gates`

findings.reason: the owner's landing note records that the byte-equality form this plan proposes is fragile (write_state normalises whitespace/attr-order), so §9 must cite the landed test and its revised invariant instead of recommending a form already superseded in-repo.
findings.text: §9 recommends adding a CI round-trip parity test asserting `render(parse(html)) == html`; that test already exists at `tests/test_schema.py:243` (`test_state_round_trip`), together with the state-level invariant and the byte-identity guard (`tests/test_schema.py:234` and `:215`)

findings.reason: an advisory recommendation that names already-superseded work invites a node to rebuild the exemplar; the plan should mark it met (as its own resolved followup `f-apa-prompt` already does) so the remaining scope is legible.
findings.text: §9 recommends "one self-describing exemplar in-repo: `docs/_exemplar-plan.html`"; that file already exists and both `skills/reckon-create/SKILL.md` and `skills/reckon-edit/SKILL.md` already point to it

findings.reason: §6 is the document's statement of the lifecycle model; describing impl as a raw item count misstates the mechanism an author must satisfy via section effort and status.
findings.text: §6 defines `impl fraction = shipped-items / items`, but the owner at `reckon/_plan_html.py:318` (`derive_impl_from_sections`) computes impl by section `effort_hours` (done over done-plus-remaining implementable, deferred sections outside the denominator), and returns nothing when records do not cover declarations

findings.reason: a second, per-phase archive path forks the landing-record mechanism the coordinator and build skills already write to, so the plan should defer to the existing owner and drop the `docs/archive/<slug>-<phase>.html` convention.
findings.text: §6 ("Per-stage archival") proposes writing a NEW file per phase under `docs/archive/<slug>-<phase>.html` (`-shipped.html`, `-12-5-landed.html`), and §4's collapse-on-landing template links a section-sized record `archive/SLUG-12-5-landed.html`; the existing owner of that concern is the cumulative record `docs/evidence/archive/<slug>-landed.html` — `reckon/evidence.py:498`, appended through `append_evidence` (`reckon/mcp.py:1714`) and `reckon/_store.py:3351`, with `AGENTS.md` (plan-lifecycle-hygiene §3) mandating one coherent record per plan and forbidding section-sized files

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan introduces no module; it documents and reuses the single existing parser/renderer pair (`reckon/_plan_html.py`).
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6/§4 propose a per-phase archive under `docs/archive/` beside the existing cumulative landing-record owner `docs/evidence/archive/<slug>-landed.html`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3's stated contract omits the `gates` section (one of six the parser recognises) and §9 re-proposes a round-trip parity test and an in-repo exemplar that already exist (`tests/test_schema.py`, `docs/_exemplar-plan.html`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no new wrapper over existing machinery is proposed; §8 keeps the MCP as the existing version-safe writer rather than layering a second one over it.
